# Chapter 9 - sketch answers {.unnumbered}

\(1\) Company lens: Revenue upside with modest risks - some churn if customers
notice, a manageable register entry. People lens: Systematic evaluation at scale
with real financial effects on individuals - price discrimination - meeting
the scoring criterion and plausibly Art. 22 territory; screening says DPIA yes.
The people lens raises the alarm, which is precisely the asymmetry the chapter
opened with. (2) Survey: Ordinary feedback data, expected, low risk - no DPIA,
recorded. Warehouse cameras including staff areas: Systematic monitoring of
employees - vulnerable in the power relationship - at least borderline, and
under Datatilsynet's guidance a DPIA is the safe answer: Do it. Loyalty
programme: Matching datasets plus location tracking at scale - two criteria,
DPIA yes. (3) Purpose: Marketing to existing customers is a real, lawful
interest - recital 47 mentions direct marketing. Necessity: Only purchase
history and email are needed; no location or browsing data. Balancing: Existing
customers reasonably expect relevant offers, so it passes - strengthened by a
clear, one-click opt-out honoured immediately, which is also what national
marketing law expects. (4) Limited-to-minimal as a system - staff decide, so
no automated decision - but the *fraud-suggestion* function scores customers,
so the GDPR side (screening, possibly a DPIA) does the heavy lifting rather than
the AI Act; the duty that applies regardless of tier is Article 4 AI literacy:
The support staff must understand what the tool can and cannot tell them. A
defensible stricter answer notes that if staff rubber-stamp the suggestions, the
"human decision" is decoration and both Art. 22 and the high-risk logic move
closer. (5) Datatilsynet or an affected customer challenges the marketing
profiling, exploiting the missing DPIA - a legal duty not performed - so
that FastGoods faces a processing ban and a fine under Art. 83, with the
campaign stopped and trust damaged as the consequence: A compliance risk, owner
the managing director, treatment "run the DPIA before the campaign launches".
